reason: Attack failed. The Norton text is in copyright and no scan opened, so I went after the wording through independent witnesses instead. Three reached separately give the same sentences, and the anthology page of extracts prints the entry heading as September 15th with no year and the opening as: BEGIN here. It is raining. I look out on the maple, where a few leaves have turned yellow, and listen to Punch, the parrot, talking to himself and to the rain ticking gently against the windows. A second witness carries the same wording and continues with the next sentence, I am here alone for the first time in weeks, so the quotation is not a paraphrase and stops at a full stop inside the paragraph. The only difference from the page is that the book sets the first word in full capitals as a typographic opening, and the shipped line prints Begin here; that is case, not wording, and the year has normalised small capitals elsewhere. Everything else checks: the journal runs from that September 15th entry to the following September, so it is the first entry; the book is W. W. Norton, 1973, well before 1999; the tag Diary is the form of the work. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, May Sarton at 1 of 3 and her one line is in month 8, so no clash in October, and she is not banned. Source line is 87 characters, leads with the name, no dash, no straight double quote. Rain, a maple and a parrot in an empty house is the month of stillness exactly, and there is nothing in it to warn a reader about. One caution for the editor rather than a fault: the evidence rests on quotation rather than on a scan, so if anyone ever opens the Norton page the heading form is the thing to look at, since some later printings head the entries with the year.
